entities.summary:
Conrad of Urach was a Cistercian monk and abbot, and Cardinal Bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina, who declined the papacy in 1227. Born in the late 12th century, Conrad rose through the ranks of the Cistercian order, becoming a prominent figure in Western Europe during the Medieval period. He played a crucial role in shaping the religious and political landscape of Italy during this time.

As a key advisor to the Holy Roman Emperor, Conrad was instrumental in negotiating the Treaty of Cortona, which helped to resolve a major conflict between the Empire and the Papal States. He also worked closely with the city of Florence, helping to promote its economic and cultural growth.

Conrad's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a significant role in shaping the development of the Cistercian order and the Catholic Church. His influence can still be felt today, particularly in the Italian city of Porto, which he helped to establish as a major center of trade and commerce.

The decline of the Holy Roman Empire and the rise of the Papal States also left their mark on Conrad's life and legacy. His decision to decline the papacy had far-reaching consequences, setting a precedent for future popes and shaping the course of European history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Conrad of Urach played a significant role in shaping the development of the Cistercian order and the Catholic Church, influencing their doctrine and practice. His decline of the papacy had far-reaching consequences, setting a precedent for future popes and shaping the course of European history.
